subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 6-month-old girl with developmental regression, an exaggerated startle response, and a cherry-red macular spot is diagnosed with Tay-Sachs disease. Her abdominal examination is normal and ultrasound shows no hepatosplenomegaly, even though an infant of the same age with Niemann-Pick disease at the same clinic has massive hepatosplenomegaly.
question: Which of the following best explains the absence of hepatosplenomegaly in this patient?

options.text: The stored substrate accumulates in hepatocytes only after weaning
The deficient enzyme is expressed exclusively in the central nervous system
The stored substrate accumulates predominantly in neurons rather than in reticuloendothelial macrophages
The defective enzyme is secreted extracellularly instead of being delivered to lysosomes
The accumulated substrate is rapidly excreted in bile

explanation_correct: In Tay-Sachs disease, GM2 ganglioside accumulates chiefly in neurons of the central nervous system, producing neurodegeneration, hyperacusis, and the cherry-red macular spot from lipid engorgement of retinal ganglion cells. The reticuloendothelial system is not a major site of storage, so the liver and spleen remain normal in size. In Niemann-Pick disease, sphingomyelin and cholesterol also accumulate in macrophages, which is why hepatosplenomegaly is prominent.

explanation_incorrect.A: Storage begins in utero and is not related to the introduction of solid food; the distribution of substrate, not the timing, explains the findings.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hexosaminidase A is expressed in essentially all cells; the difference reflects where the substrate accrues, not enzyme expression.
explanation_incorrect.D: Extracellular secretion of lysosomal enzymes is the defect in I-cell disease, not Tay-Sachs disease.
explanation_incorrect.E: GM2 ganglioside is not excreted in bile; it accumulates within neurons and their lysosomes.

educationalObjective: Tay-Sachs disease lacks hepatosplenomegaly because GM2 ganglioside accumulates predominantly in central nervous system neurons rather than in reticuloendothelial macrophages.
